create.name: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
create.bio:
Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche is a lama of Bön, Tibet's native spiritual tradition, and was among the first teachers to bring its Dzogchen teachings to Western students. Born in Amritsar in 1961 to a family that had left Tibet two years before, he entered Menri Monastery in northern India as a boy, was recognised there as the reincarnation of a meditation master, and completed the monastery's eleven-year course of study, earning his geshe degree in 1986. He first taught in Italy at the invitation of Chögyal Namkhai Norbu, then came to Rice University in Texas as a Rockefeller fellow, and has made the United States his home since the early 1990s.

In 1992 he founded Ligmincha, which has grown into an international network of retreat centres and practice groups, and he later started The 3 Doors for people who want this kind of meditation outside a religious frame. He now lives as a householder and teaches in a warm, conversational way, with everyday examples. His subjects include dream and sleep yoga, breath and movement practices, sacred sound and resting in open awareness. Among his books are The Tibetan Yogas of Dream and Sleep, plus Wonders of the Natural Mind on Dzogchen. He offers free webcasts, online courses and retreats across the Americas, Europe and Asia.

books.title: The Tibetan Yogas of Dream and Sleep: Practices for Awakening
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: His best-known book, first published by Snow Lion in 1998 and reissued by Shambhala. It sets out the Bön approach to dreaming and to sleeping with awareness, with step-by-step practices for the night and for the day.

books.title: Wonders of the Natural Mind: The Essence of Dzogchen in the Native Bon Tradition of Tibet
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: An introduction to Dzogchen as it is taught in Bön, with a foreword by the Dalai Lama. It covers the history of the tradition, its view of the nature of mind and the meditation that follows from it.

books.title: Healing with Form, Energy, and Light: The Five Elements in Tibetan Shamanism, Tantra, and Dzogchen
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A study of earth, water, fire, air and space as they appear in Tibetan shamanic, tantric and Dzogchen teaching. It includes practices for working with each element in the body, the energy and the mind.

books.title: Tibetan Sound Healing: Seven Guided Practices to Clear Obstacles, Cultivate Positive Qualities, and Uncover Your Inherent Wisdom
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A short practice book from Sounds True built around the five warrior seed syllables of the Bön tradition. Each sound is linked with a centre in the body and a quality of mind, and guided audio comes with it.

books.title: Awakening the Sacred Body
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A Hay House book on Tibetan yogas of breath and movement, centred on the nine purification breathings and the five tsa lung exercises. It explains how each movement opens a different energy centre and supports meditation.

books.title: Awakening the Luminous Mind: Tibetan Meditation for Inner Peace and Joy
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A plain guide to three refuges found in stillness, silence and spaciousness. It shows readers how to step back from busy thoughts and feelings and rest in open awareness during ordinary life.

books.title: The True Source of Healing: How the Ancient Tibetan Practice of Soul Retrieval Can Transform and Enrich Your Life
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: His adaptation of the Bön practice of soul retrieval for modern readers. It draws on the five elements and on inner refuge to help readers reconnect with vitality, warmth and a sense of belonging.

books.title: Spontaneous Creativity: Meditations for Manifesting Your Positive Qualities
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A book about letting creative action grow out of open awareness rather than effort. It offers meditations and reflections on clearing what gets in the way and allowing good qualities to show up in daily life.

books.title: Tibetan Yogas of Body, Speech, and Mind
books.author: Tenzin Wangyal Rinpoche
books.description: A Snow Lion book that presents Bön practices for each of the three doors of body, speech and mind. It brings together posture and movement, breath and sound, and meditation on the nature of mind.

courses.title: Tibetan Dream Yoga
courses.description: A five-day residential workshop at Esalen in Big Sur on the Tibetan practice of dream yoga. Rinpoche looks at how waking, dreaming and dying relate, gives the preparations for sleep and teaches ways of becoming lucid in dreams.

courses.title: A Journey to Self-Realization
courses.description: A two-week self-paced online workshop built on Who Am I?, a poem Rinpoche wrote from his own practice. Short video sessions move from the basics of meditation to letting a fixed sense of self loosen in open awareness.

courses.title: Tibetan Sound Healing
courses.description: A self-paced online course in which Rinpoche guides the practice of the five warrior seed syllables. Each syllable is sounded with attention on a centre in the body, as a way of clearing obstacles and connecting with positive qualities.

courses.title: Sleep Yoga
courses.description: A four-week guided online course drawn from Rinpoche's teaching on falling asleep with awareness. It combines breathing, simple postures and guided practice for evening and morning, with online discussion; the course runs more than once a year.

courses.title: The Practice in Six Sessions
courses.description: A set of recorded teachings on the Six Sessions practice that Rinpoche created. It lays out a complete daily meditation practice from the Bön tradition that can be followed at home.

free_resources.title: Starting a Meditation Practice, From the Bön Tradition of Tibet
free_resources.description: A free two-part online course for people who want to start meditating every day. Rinpoche gives simple instructions for sitting, breathing and settling the mind, drawn from the Bön tradition.

free_resources.title: Focusing and Calming Your Mind: The Tibetan Practice of Zhiné
free_resources.description: A free two-week self-guided online workshop on GlideWing teaching calm abiding, the Tibetan practice of steady attention. It suits beginners but also works as a refresher for experienced meditators.

free_resources.title: Living With Joy, Dying in Peace
free_resources.description: A free self-paced course on letting go of attachment so that each day can be met with joy and death with calm. It treats living and dying as one continuous journey, as the Tibetan traditions do.

free_resources.title: Transforming Your World Through Service
free_resources.description: A free course built from a 2016 series of live webcasts by Rinpoche. It looks at service to others as part of spiritual growth and how open awareness can shape the way we help.
